name: Domestic helper transfer agencies
summary: How expats use MDW transfer agencies in Singapore when hiring an already-in-country helper — documentation, probation norms, and how transfers differ from first-time overseas hires.
body:
Transfer hires place a helper already in Singapore with a new employer. Agencies intermediate matching, MOM paperwork, and sometimes short handovers. This is different from first-time overseas recruitment timelines and costs.

## Why transfers appeal
- Faster start than overseas pipelines
- Prior Singapore experience (English, public transport, condo rules)
- Shorter uncertainty on cultural fit — still not zero risk

Prior employment disputes, rest-day norms, and loan/salary histories still need careful interviews.

## Process checkpoints
- Verify work-pass eligibility and transfer consent steps on MOM channels
- Clear safety orientation and house rules in writing
- Medical check requirements on transfer
- Agency fees vs direct-employer responsibilities
- Exit/cancellation planning if the match fails

Use official MOM guidance as source of truth; agency WhatsApp summaries go stale.

## How to choose
Prefer agencies that allow proper interviews, disclose prior placement context lawfully, and do not pressure same-day signatures. Cross-check fee schedules and refund rules. Pair with the hiring-helper guide for levy, insurance, and rest-day baselines.

## Practical tip
Check references where possible and run a paid trial period with documented expectations. Keep copies of the employment contract and safety agreement in shared cloud storage for both spouses.
